sentences.text: Striatolamia is an extinct genus of sharks in the family Odontaspididae, named for the 'striped' pattern on its teeth.
The front teeth featured elongated crowns with striations on the inner face and small side cusplets.
Individuals of this genus could reach a total length of about 350 centimeters.
The genus was formally described by Glikman in 1964.
Fossil teeth and vertebrae have been found worldwide.
While the family Odontaspididae is the current classification, other authors have previously assigned Striatolamia to the families Mitsukurinidae and Striatolamiidae.
These sharks lived from the Early Paleocene to the Late Miocene, between 61.7 and 10.3 million years ago.
They inhabited waters with low salinity.
Some records list the time range for Striatolamia as Campanian to Messinian, from 83.6 to 5.333 million years ago.
